headline: Waste Management trash and recycling contract tabled to special meeting on November 9.
summary: The five-year contract would start July 1, 2027, with a first-year annual rate of $2,689,790. Members wanted more time to review it, and the next step is a workshop and special meeting on November 9. Earlier, the council approved a one-year moratorium on data centers and a request for state and federal funds for the Arlington neighborhood water project.
decisions: Approved appointment of Jeffrey Farrely as Superintendent of Building Maintenance, unanimous.
Approved appointment of Michael Welch to the Conservation Commission, unanimous.
Approved joint resolution asking for state and federal funds for the Arlington neighborhood water project, unanimous.
Approved public service grant 31358901 for a new National Grid pole on Taft Avenue, unanimous.
Approved C-27-40 contract with United Compressor & Pump Services for $32,891.63 sewer pump replacement, unanimous.
Approved C-27-41 contract with SHI International for $38,684.21 Cityworks software subscription, unanimous.
Approved C-27-42 grant-funded data cataloger position for Jessica Powers at $72,800, unanimous.
Approved C-27-43 engineering contract with Andrew Brockway & Associates for $29,000, 8-1.
Approved C-27-44 contract with Northeast Behavioral Health for $138,129 mental health and jail diversion program, unanimous.
Tabled C-27-45 trash and recycling contract with Waste Management to a special meeting on November 9.
Approved resolution calling for reopening of federal investigation into former Methuen Police leadership, 4-3.
Approved $27,999.02 bulletproof vest partnership grant, unanimous.
Approved acceptance of $48,759.90 federal municipal road safety grant, unanimous.
Approved accepting Planet Fitness equipment gift for the fire department, unanimous.
Approved amendment restoring data centers to the zoning table of uses, unanimous.
Approved temporary one-year moratorium on data centers, as amended, unanimous.
Approved $36,000 Sustainable Materials Recovery Program grant, unanimous.
Approved amendment changing the $2,000 award to American Legion Post 122 for the Veterans Day Parade band.
Approved $33,000 transfer from the Edwin J. Castle Fund for various awards, with one abstention.
Denied resolution on Group Insurance Commission eligibility, unanimous no.
Approved home rule petition on paving unaccepted ways, 8-1.
Tabled industrial zoning ordinance TO-26-22 for a joint public hearing, unanimous.
discussion: Waste Management contract: Members asked about truck purchases, the city's barrels, and the five-year term, and said they wanted time to review it. The mayor's presentation estimated truck rental costs of $100,000 to $200,000 if the vote was delayed, and the company offered to cover about $165,000 in rental fees if the contract was signed.

Condo trash service: Public speakers from condo communities said owners pay taxes but do not get curbside trash or recycling pickup. A housing authority director said the cost estimate for the authority's trash service was overstated and asked to stay in the city contract.

Federal investigation letter: Public speakers urged the council to sign a letter asking federal officials to reopen the investigation into former police leadership. Speakers asked two members to step aside because of ties to a 2017 contract, and two members said they had sought state Ethics Commission advice and did not vote.

Arlington water project: The mayor said the city has invested over $13 million in phase one and that the remaining phases are estimated at $88 million. He said a $38 million application to the Commonwealth State Revolving Fund was rejected and listed $5 million in state funds, $3 million in federal funds, and $10 million in proposed bond earmarks.

Group Insurance Commission eligibility: The mayor said joining the state GIC would save at least $11.2 million in premiums through fiscal year 2030. Members debated whether part-time elected officials should get city health coverage, and the solicitor said elected officials are eligible under state rules regardless of hours worked.
